sections.skill: Use AI to widen options, then choose and check

questions.prompt: What is an AI tool especially good at during brainstorming?

choices.text: Guaranteeing every idea is legal and affordable
Knowing your schedule and budget automatically
Choosing the single right option for your situation
Producing many options quickly

questions.correct_answer: Producing many options quickly
questions.intro: AI tools are good at WIDENING OPTIONS: brainstorming names, ideas for a project, possible schedules, or different ways to approach a problem. They can produce many options quickly, including ones you might not think of. Your job is to NARROW and CHOOSE: check each option against your real constraints (time, money, rules, people involved), drop the ones that do not fit, and verify any facts, such as whether a venue exists or an activity is allowed. A plan from a tool is a draft. Asking for options "with pros and cons" or "ranked by cost" makes choosing easier.

questions.prompt: How does a menu help?

choices.text: It pays the bill
It cooks the food for you
It decides your order based on your allergies
It shows options you might not think of

questions.correct_answer: It shows options you might not think of
questions.intro: A restaurant MENU shows many dishes, which helps you think of things you might not have ordered. But the menu does not know you are allergic to peanuts, that you have 20 dollars, or that you are not very hungry. You still choose. An AI brainstorm is like a big menu of ideas: helpful for seeing possibilities, but you must pick based on what you know about your own needs, and confirm details, like whether a dish is still available.

sections.title: Apply it

sections.skill: Catch hidden assumptions and impossible plans

questions.prompt: A day plan lists a 2 p.m. museum visit across town and a 2 p.m. lunch downtown. What is wrong?

choices.text: Two activities are scheduled at the same time
Museums are always closed at 2 p.m.
Lunch cannot be eaten downtown
Nothing; plans with many activities are always fine

questions.correct_answer: Two activities are scheduled at the same time
questions.intro: Brainstorming has traps. Tools tend toward common, safe ideas, so ask explicitly for unusual options if you want them. A long list can feel complete even when it misses the option that fits you best, so add your own ideas too. Plans can assume things that are not true for you: free weekends, a car, a budget, good weather. And a schedule can look tidy while being impossible, such as two activities at the same time or no travel time. Read a plan the way you would read a friend's suggestion: useful, but checked.

questions.prompt: A travel plan has no time for getting between places. What should you add?

choices.text: A longer list of restaurants
Realistic travel time
More activities to fill every possible minute of the day
Nothing; travel is instant

questions.correct_answer: Realistic travel time
